title: BER: get rid of WTAP_FILE_TYPE_SUBTYPE_BER.
description:
Save a copy of the pathname used to open a file in the wtap structure.
This allows the BER file reader to put a pointer to it in the
pseudo-header; it also would allow file readers to attempt to read
"associated" files that have the same name as the file, but with a
different extension.

Instead of having cf_open() special-case BER files, and calling a
routine in the BER dissector to specify the file name to the dissector,
have separate dissectors for "dissect packet payload as BER" and
"dissect a file as BER", and have the latter get the pathname of the
file from the pseudo-header and determine the ASN.1 syntax from that.

(Side-effect - this means that you can now dissect a BER file, and have
the syntax be determined by the file extension, in TShark as well; the
above cf_open() special-casing was *not* done in TShark, so it didn't
work before.  Now the application code doesn't need to do any of that,
so it works in TShark as well as Wireshark.)

This (further) broke Decode As for BER.

Originally, the BER Decode As functionality allowed for both an attempt to determine the syntax based on file extension as well as specifying the syntax to use if there wasn't an known extension / to override it. After this, the `file_syntax` is always used for BER files, but it should fall back to the `decode_as_syntax` value.

Except that the BER Decode As table (like the DCERPC one) has never really been adapted to the "new" Decode As (6-10 years ago).

The BER syntax dissector table is intended to be a custom-functioning FT_STRING table where, when used for Decode As, the FT_STRING is mostly ignored (but used for display) and is really used like a Payload dissector table to dissect all *unknown* BER. Except that the table serves a double purpose by allowing registration of OIDs through an OID-to-syntax table. Those register a string, then the string is looked up in the other table.

Probably, starting from scratch, the one would be a simple Payload dissector table, and the OID UAT would reference dissectors directly instead of indirectly looking up in the other table.

> Originally, the BER Decode As functionality allowed for both an attempt to determine the syntax based on file extension

Meaning "allowed the user to specify the syntax that corresponds to a particular file extension"?

`register_ber_oid_syntax()` is... not a very clear name, as what it registers is a *file extension*, and there appear to be precisely zero OIDs involved in that call (and the second argument always appears to be NULL).  The third argument might b a *name* that is registered, along with an OID, a protocol ID, and a dissector, by `register_ber_oid_dissector()`, or registered with a protocol ID and a dissector by `register_ber_syntax_dissector()`.

So, yes, the way we handle BER dissection should be redone. For example, should OIDs have names, or should names just be for dissectors?

> Meaning "allowed the user to specify the syntax that corresponds to a particular file extension"?

Yes. Some explanation in the original commit 2fd7d2c62078813f44e78f0b4b9f8b0e6e5928fb, but it's all a bit confusing. It doesn't really work currently.
